structured.answer: I'd go with option 1, "החברה בראש השורה". It opens straight on "עוקב מדד s&p 500", the thing my friends talk about, with the company name in bold on each row, so I could see מנורה מבטחים at 0.52% and 13.79% at the top and know what to look at. I'm fairly sure about the option, but I'm not sure what this "קופת גמל להשקעה" thing actually is.

stuck.why: The three numbered tabs (1, 2, 3) made it clear these were choices, but I didn't get what 'טבלת חברות מול סוגים' would be until I scrolled to it. The 'מומלץ' badge almost pulled me there without looking.
A really long list of הראל and then מור tracks, mostly bonds and things I don't know. I lost track of where the S&P one was and wanted to close it.
A wall of percentages that all look the same (0.5x–0.7x) on brown squares. I guessed darker or orange means more expensive, but I'm not sure. No returns, so nothing told me which one actually grows.
Some S&P rows have no return figure, just 'פחות מ-3 שנים'. I'm not sure if that means they're bad or just new.

findings.what: The 'מומלץ' option (3) is a grid of near-identical percentages with colours I can't read and no returns. I'd only take it because it says recommended, not because I understood it.
Fees are only in small percents. Nothing in shekels, so 0.52% vs 0.71% feels like nothing.
The company-grouped list is endless and mostly tracks I don't know. You have to dig to find S&P.
Lots of S&P rows show 'פחות מ-3 שנים' instead of a number, which made those look worse or suspicious.
Two fee lines per row (מהחיסכון / מההפקדות). Confusing which one matters.
The rings and the 'מניות / מט"ח' percents are unexplained. I just ignored them.
No 'what do I do next' button anywhere, only small arrows at the left edge of the rows, which I barely noticed.
